summary_html: The **Protect Our Kids Act (PL 112-275)** created a national commission to study child-fatality prevention. Project Milk Carton cross-references its findings with state fatality data to expose non-implementation.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: In a suit over a child's death, the Court held that a public children services agency and its employees owe no R.C. 2151.421(A)(1)(a) duty to cross-report an incoming referral to law enforcement, that R.C. 2919.22 does not expressly impose liability on them, and that employee immunity is lost only for recklessness, which requires a perverse disregard of a known risk rather than mere negligence.
key_cases.relevance: The case illustrates why fatality review rather than tort litigation is the practical accountability route in Ohio.
key_cases.quote: a public children services agency and its employees, upon receipt of a case referral, do not have a duty under R.C. 2151.421(A)(1)(a) to cross-report the case to a law-enforcement agency

key_cases.case_name: Yates v. Mansfield Bd. of Edn.
key_cases.holding: A board of education may be held liable under former R.C. 2744.02(B)(5) when its failure to report a teacher's sexual abuse of one student in violation of R.C. 2151.421 proximately results in the same teacher's sexual abuse of a different student.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion articulates the preventive purpose of mandatory reporting that fatality and near-fatality reviews are meant to enforce.
key_cases.quote: R.C. 2151.421(A)(1)(a) requires designated persons to "immediately report" their "knowledge or suspicion" that a child "has suffered or faces a threat of suffering" any injury indicative of abuse or neglect

key_cases.holding: County children services board investigation records kept under R.C. 5153.17 and 2151.141 are 'official records' subject to the sealing provisions of R.C. 2953.52, and the prosecutor who failed to object timely could not relitigate the sealing order later.
key_cases.relevance: It defines the statutory character of the investigation file that fatality and systemic reviewers must work from.
key_cases.quote: records of a county children services board investigation made pursuant to R.C. 5153.17 and 2151.141 are "official records" within the ambit of the sealing provisions of R.C. 2953.52
